A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CTMSR work. All 20 pages of each version, including equations, tables, figures and the supplementary material, are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original super-resolution evaluations, runtime measurements and ablations in Tables 1–8, with qualitative results in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: v3 retains the original benchmark evaluations, runtime measurements, ablations and qualitative results in Tables 1–8 and the accompanying figures.

M1.justification: CTMSR's architecture, CT and DTM objectives, and inference procedure remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 line 7 changes the computed pair from x_t, x_{t+1} to x_{t-1}, x_t, aligning the pseudocode with the method already specified in Equation 10 and supplementary Algorithm 2.

E1.justification: Both versions use ImageNet training data and evaluate super-resolution on ImageNet-Test, RealSR and RealSet65. The appendix retains the same dataset and scenario coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding experiments, including the main SR baselines, the SDS ablation comparator, and OSEDiff and AddSR in supplementary Table 8.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 revises the second-stage CT-plus-DTM training budget from 10K to 2K iterations after the same 500K CT pretraining iterations. Other settings remain unchanged, including the 10K ablation budget in Section 4.3. This is a reported protocol revision; the PDFs do not establish whether experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The DTM, no-DTM and SDS ablations in Section 4.3 and Tables 4–7 are retained unchanged. The CLIPIQA case study in supplementary Figure 6 and the additional visual comparisons are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Statistical and uncertainty reporting practices remain unchanged throughout the main text and appendix.

E6.justification: All result entries in Tables 1–8 and qualitative examples remain unchanged. For example, CTMSR retains ImageNet-Test MUSIQ 60.142 and the 48 ms runtime in Table 3. The revised training-budget statement does not establish a demonstrated efficiency or performance improvement.

T1.justification: The PF-ODE derivations, trajectory-matching mathematics and supplementary schedule definitions in Equations 1–25 are unchanged. The Algorithm 1 indexing correction aligns with existing mathematics and introduces no new definition, derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims: distillation-free one-step SR through consistency training, improved realism through DTM, and competitive perceptual quality with low inference latency.

C2.justification: The interpretation of DTM's distribution-matching benefits is unchanged. The appendix retains the same discussion of CLIPIQA favoring noise or artifacts and the applicability constraints of Stable Diffusion backbones.

D1.justification: The documented second-stage iteration count changes from 10K to 2K, and Algorithm 1 corrects the timestep pair needed by its loss calculation. Other implementation details, supplementary training schedules, hardware information and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Both versions contain the same 50 references and the same positioning relative to consistency models, diffusion acceleration, distillation and prior SR methods. Bibliography reflow introduces no citation or positioning changes.

P1.justification: v3 reverses the author order of Kexuan Shi and Xingyu Zhou, updates the arXiv version/date text, and adds a funding acknowledgement after the conclusion. Apart from the localized technical corrections, the prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added acknowledgement shifts the bibliography layout across pages 9–11. Figures 1–13 and Tables 1–8 retain their displays, captions and placement; the supplementary pages are visually unchanged.

improvement.justification: Correcting Algorithm 1's timestep pair improves internal consistency. However, v3 specifies 2K second-stage iterations in Section 4.1 while retaining 10K in Section 4.3 and identical final-model scores, without explaining whether these reflect different runs or a corrected setting. This creates uncertainty about reproducibility that cannot be reliably weighed against the small pseudocode improvement; the remaining scientific evidence is unchanged.
